properties.title: Spanish election threatens to blow up Brussels’ political balance
properties.summary: BRUSSELS — A defeat for Pedro Sánchez in Spain’s snap election risks destabilizing the EU by putting the Socialists and Democrats on the back foot in Brussels and pushing them into a more confrontational stance. Sánchez, the only Socialist-aligned leader currently running a large EU country, has provided a center-left counterweight to decisions in a Council largely dominated by the center right. properties.title: France’s debt troubles stir memories of the euro crisis
properties.summary: France’s borrowing costs are surging as investors around the world wake up to the risk of a full-blown public debt crisis in Europe’s second-largest economy. Stress in financial markets has now started to spread beyond its borders, raising fears that political dysfunction in France could cause a broader, regional problem. properties.title: Romanian president signs law regulating bear population cull
properties.summary: In recent years Romania has increasingly seen bears wandering into towns and villages, and the number of bear attacks has risen sharply.

properties.title: Diplomat is Romania’s fourth prime ministerial candidate in five months
properties.summary: A senior diplomat will try to form a new government as Romania’s prime minister, in an attempt to end a five-month stalemate that threatens the country’s economic and political stability. President Nicușor Dan named Luca Niculescu, secretary of state in the foreign ministry, as prime minister-designate on Monday. properties.title: Bosnia awaits for final general election results as preliminary count remains unclear
properties.summary: Around 3.4 million eligible voters in Bosnia headed to the polls to choose the three members of the country’s multi-ethnic presidency, lawmakers for the national Parliament, and heads of institutions for the country’s two entities.
